proposals.name: Repair the KP14 'truth': regenerate integ_results.npz and G_func.csv, and fix the H/L regime convention
proposals.one_line: The shipped quadrature file returns exactly 0 for E_t[G] over the entire eps region the panel occupies, so every reported KP14 number (rp, cond_var, max_sr, sdf_ret, the 'true SDF weights') is a numerical artifact — nothing can be evaluated until this is fixed.
proposals.economic_story: This is not an economic change, it is a precondition. KP14's economics are that assets in place earn gamma_x*sigma_x = 8.97%/yr and growth options earn 8.97 - alph*|gamma_z*sigma_z| = 2.03%/yr, so the true cross-section is rp_i = gamma_x*sigma_x*dt + alph*gamma_z*sigma_z*dt*(PVGO_i/P_i) with a 6.94%/yr AIP-vs-growth-option spread. Right now the code delivers rp_i = -PVGO_i/P_i (R^2=0.90 on the PVGO share, slope -0.95), mean -38.5%/yr with the WRONG SIGN and a cross-sectional sd 173x the correct value, because term2 (the PVGO continuation value, panel_functions_kp14.py:193) is multiplied by E_t[G] ~ 1e-53. That, and not any economic feature, is what produces the negative Sharpes (-2.64 FF, -5.35 FM) and max_sr = 34.66/yr against the model's own HJ bound of 0.774/yr. A referee reading the current KP14 table is reading noise.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: No direct DKKM gain — this proposal buys correctness, not headroom, and I say so explicitly. Its indirect mechanisms: (i) it restores PVGO/P from 0.040 to ~0.55 (see arithmetic), which restores beta_z = alph*share to a real second factor with p10-p90 premium spread ~2.7%/yr instead of 0.48%/yr; (ii) it flips rp positive so that the Sharpe metric SR = SR* x cos_Sigma(w, w*) stops being dominated by a sign flip and the DKKM/FF/FM ordering becomes interpretable; (iii) every other proposal below is scored against these true moments, so all of them are uninterpretable without it.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: Not applicable — this is a bug fix, not a source of DKKM advantage. Stated honestly: on its own this proposal will NOT create a DKKM-over-FF/FM gap. After the fix, PVGO share is still (to first order) an exact affine function of book-to-market — I verified VAP_i/book_i = (1/alpha) x [K-weighted mean of z_t*A(eps_t,u_j)/(z_{t_j}*A(eps_{t_j},1))] with cross-sectional sd of only 3.2% of its mean (measured: mean 1.2489, sd 0.0401 at N=200, t=210, vs 1/alpha = 1.1765). So share_i = 1 - v_i*bm_i with v_i almost constant, beta_z is affine in bm, and FM spans it exactly. Expect FF ~ FM ~ DKKM after this fix, all with SHARPE ~0.15-0.22/month and the right sign.

proposals.name: Investment-specific technology SPACE: replace the scalar IST shock z by K priced technology-domain shocks over an observable 2-D technology map
proposals.one_line: Make z a K-dimensional, spatially-correlated field over an observable technology coordinate theta_i, with domain-specific prices of risk gamma_k — turning KP14's single priced growth-option factor into ~100 priced factors whose loadings are share_i x bump_k(theta_i), a product no linear-in-characteristics rule can form.
proposals.economic_story: KP14's z is investment-specific technological change, identified empirically from the relative price of equipment. It is a stylized fact — not a stretch — that IST progress is domain-specific: semiconductors, communications equipment, industrial machinery, biotech instrumentation and structures have wildly different equipment-price trends and different exposures to the same innovations (Papanikolaou 2011; Kogan-Papanikolaou-Stoffman; Greenwood-Hercowitz-Krusell's equipment-price series is a weighted average of exactly such components). Firms hold growth options in a technology neighbourhood, and technologically proximate firms' options move together (Hoberg-Phillips TNIC, Bloom-Schankerman-Van Reenen technology space, Lee-Sun-Wang-Zhang technology links). Whether an IST innovation in a domain is good or bad news for the incumbents holding options there — cost reduction vs. creative destruction — differs by domain, so the price of risk gamma_k differs by domain. The scalar-z KP14 is the K=1 special case. This is the single most defensible way to raise the number of priced aggregate shocks from 2 to ~100 while leaving KP14's identity (growth options load on IST, assets in place load on neutral productivity) completely intact.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: With K priced IST factors the true conditional MVE weight is w*_i = [gamma_x*sigma_x*dt + alph*share_i*sigma_z*(p(theta_i) . c_t)] / d_i, where p(theta_i) in R^K is the firm's technology loading vector and c_t is a month-specific K-vector determined by the realized cross-section. So the priced part of w* is share_i x g_t(theta_i) / d_i with g_t(.) = p(.) . c_t an arbitrary smooth function on the technology torus with ~K degrees of freedom. The attainable Sharpe of any estimator whose stock-weight function lies in a function class F is SR^2 = gamma_x^2 + sum_k gamma_k^2 x (fraction of R^K reachable), and the reachable fraction is (number of independent modes of g that F can express)/K. Formally: the map a -> exposure vector e_k = sum_i w_a(x_i) alph share_i sigma_z p_ik has rank equal to dim(F restricted to functions of theta, times share). FM has rank ~3 ({1, theta1, theta2} — it can multiply by bm, which is affine in share, but cannot multiply by a nonlinear function of theta). DKKM's RFF spans smooth functions of all 7 characteristics jointly, so it reaches all quadratic (6) modes at the coded bandwidth and ~45 modes with the bandwidth rescaled. This is a first-order (not O(1/N)) loss for FM: it is a loss of factor Sharpe, not of diversification.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: FM's investable set each month is exactly {X_t a : a in R^{L+1}} with X_t = [1, size, bm, agr, roe, mom, theta1, theta2] (fama_functions.py:158-160 builds P = X pinvh(X'X) on raw chars), i.e. its stock-weight FUNCTION is a fixed LINEAR functional of the characteristics, identical in every month. It therefore cannot produce share_i x g(theta_i) for any nonconstant g, and cannot produce any nonlinear function of theta at all. The image of its exposure map in R^K is a subspace of dimension at most L+1 = 8; with K=100 it can harvest at most 8/100 of sum_k gamma_k^2 outside the common direction. FF is strictly worse: fama_functions.py:82-104 builds, per characteristic, a value-weighted 2x3 tercile double sort with size, so its weight function is mve_i x (piecewise-constant on a 2x3 grid of (size-tercile-of-median-split, char-tercile)). It contains size x char interactions and nothing else — no theta1 x theta2 interaction, no share x theta interaction, and only tercile resolution in theta (2 modes). Its exposure-map rank is 7. Neither can express a product of two non-size characteristics, which is the minimum requirement here.

proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation:
BUMP NORMALIZATION. With Gaussian bumps phi_k(theta)=exp(-||theta-c_k||_torus^2/(2h^2)) on a 2-D torus with K=1/h^2 centers, sum_k phi_k -> (1/h^2)(2 pi h^2) = 2 pi and sum_k phi_k^2 -> (1/h^2)(pi h^2) = pi, so with L2-normalized loadings p = phi/||phi||_2 the quantity q = sum_k p_k = 2*pi/sqrt(pi) = 2*sqrt(pi) = 3.5449, independent of K and h. I verified numerically: K=100,h=0.10 gives q = 3.54490 +/- 0.00019 across 20,000 random theta; K=64,h=0.125 gives 3.54452. L2 normalization is what preserves each firm's own z process EXACTLY as in the current model (drift mu_z, vol sigma_z), which is what keeps A_0..A_3, C and the eps machinery untouched.
FIRM-LEVEL PRICE OF IST RISK. Firm i's effective price is g_i = p(theta_i).gamma, with mean q*GAMMA_Z_BAR and sd SIGMA_GAMMA_Z (since ||p||_2 = 1). Set the mean to -0.175, i.e. HALF of KP14's -0.35, which preserves the sign and the economics of the value premium while buying transversality headroom. Hence GAMMA_Z_BAR = -0.175/3.5449 = -0.049366. Set SIGMA_GAMMA_Z = 0.30, i.e. the cross-domain dispersion of IST risk prices is 1.7x their mean level, so ~28% of technology domains carry a positive IST premium (creative-destruction domains). 
TRANSVERSALITY IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT AND IS WHY ALPHA MUST FALL. rho_i = r + gamma_x sigma_x - mu_x - alph(mu_z - g_i sigma_z - 0.5 sigma_z^2) - 0.5 alph^2 sigma_z^2 (config.py:270-272), which I evaluate as rho(g) = base + alph*sigma_z*g. At alpha=0.85 (alph=5.667): rho = 0.085169 + 0.198333 g, so rho = 0 at g = -0.4294 — only 0.079 below the current gamma_z = -0.35. ANY meaningful cross-domain dispersion blows up the growth-option value. At alpha=0.80 (alph=4): rho = 0.10235 + 0.14 g, zero at g = -0.7311. At alpha=0.75 (alph=3): rho = 0.111025 + 0.105 g, zero at g = -1.0574. With mean -0.175 and sd 0.30 truncated at 2.5 sd, the worst firm has g = -0.925 and rho = 0.0139 > 0. SAFE. alpha=0.75 is well inside the empirical range for returns to scale (Basu-Fernald, Cooper-Haltiwanger report 0.7-0.9); alph = alpha/(1-alpha) falls from 5.667 to 3.000 and KP14_C = alpha^{1/(1-alpha)}(1/alpha - 1) from 0.05972 to 0.10547.
RESULTING SHARPE ACCOUNTING (annualized, K=100). Total: SR*^2 = gamma_x^2 + K(GAMMA_Z_BAR^2 + SIGMA_GAMMA_Z^2) = 0.4761 + 100(0.002437 + 0.09) = 9.720, SR* = 3.118/yr = 0.900/month. This lands exactly on DKKM's real-data attainable Sharpe of 3.7. The 'common' IST direction K*GAMMA_Z_BAR^2 = 0.244 is spanned by everyone; the unspanned budget is K*SIGMA_GAMMA_Z^2 = 9.00. FM (m=3 theta-modes): SR = sqrt(0.4761+0.244+0.03*9.00) = 0.995/yr = 0.319 of SR* — right on top of FF6's real-data 0.74-1.2. DKKM at the CODED bandwidth (effective dictionary rank ~16, giving ~6 quadratic theta-modes): SR = 1.122/yr = 0.360 of SR*. DKKM with GAMMA_GRID rescaled by sqrt(130/7)=4.31 (effective rank ~78, ~45 theta-modes): SR = 2.184/yr = 0.701 of SR*.
WHY K MUST BE LARGE. I checked the small-K version: K=6 with a 1-D theta gives SR* = 1.03/yr, FM 0.841, DKKM-coded 0.942 — a 1.12x gap. The gap scales as sqrt(m_DKKM/m_FM) and needs K >> L to open up. K=100 on 1000 firms leaves ~10 firms per cell but ~30-50 within one bandwidth, so each domain's mimicking portfolio diversifies idio risk from 5%/mo to ~0.9%/mo against a factor exposure of alph*share*sigma_z/sqrt(12) = 3*0.5*0.035/3.464 = 1.5%/mo — 74% systematic, so the factors are genuinely spannable. K=64 (h=0.125) is the safer choice if N is ever reduced.

proposals.name: Historical-cost book value plus the characteristics KP14 already generates (capital vintage/age, project count, cash-flow volatility, investment intensity)
proposals.one_line: Stop marking book equity to current replacement cost — record it at the historical prices actually paid — and add the vintage, count and volatility characteristics the state already contains, so that PVGO share becomes bm x g(age) rather than an exact affine function of bm.
proposals.economic_story: panel_functions_kp14.py:144 sets book = (x_t/z_t) * sum_j K_j, i.e. it revalues every project's capital at TODAY'S investment price. Real book equity is historical cost: the firm records what it paid, which is exactly the cash outflow the model already writes down at line 157, -K_j * x_{t_j}/z_{t_j}. The gap between the two is the source of a large fraction of the real value premium's information content (Fama-French have always argued B/M works partly because book is a stale, historical-cost anchor; the whole 'q vs. B/M' literature is about this wedge). Making book historical-cost simultaneously (i) makes bm a mixture of value and capital vintage rather than a pure valuation ratio, and (ii) makes capital age a genuinely informative, separately observable characteristic — which is exactly what it is in real data (accumulated depreciation / gross PP&E is a standard char). The other three additions are quantities the model already simulates: number of live projects (segment/establishment count), trailing investment intensity (R&D + capex over assets, the observable proxy for lambda_f and the H/L arrival regime), and trailing cash-flow volatility (the observable proxy for d_i).

Hence share_i = 1 - v_i * bm_i with v_i almost constant, so beta_z = alph*share is an AFFINE function of bm and FM spans the entire z-channel exactly. Under historical-cost book, v_i acquires the extra factor (x_t/z_t)/(K-weighted mean of x_{t_j}/z_{t_j}), whose log has cross-firm sd approximately sd(log(x/z) increment) x sqrt(E[age]) / sqrt(n_eff) = 0.1346 x sqrt(10) / sqrt(6) = 0.174 — a 5.4x increase in the multiplicative wedge, and one whose cross-firm variation is driven by capital AGE, which is now an observable characteristic. So beta_z,i = alph*(1 - bm_i * exp(c0 + c1*age_i + eta_i)): a product of bm with a nonlinear function of age. The true MVE weight inherits it. Separately, cfvol makes 1/d_i learnable directly rather than only through size, which is what the D^{-1} tilt needs to be a multiplier on the unspanned premium in Proposals 2 and 6.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: The required object is bm_i x exp(c1 * age_i), a product of two NON-SIZE characteristics. FM produces only a0 + a1*bm + a2*age + ...; the bilinear term bm*age is orthogonal to its span by construction (its span is literally the column space of [1, chars], fama_functions.py:158-160). DKKM's RFF, even at the coded bandwidth where sd(Wx) = 0.53 and the dictionary is ~86% quadratic in the chars, contains every pairwise product including bm x age. This is the one nonlinearity that the CURRENT estimator configuration can already reach, which is why this proposal has the best impact-per-line of any economic change here.

proposals.name: Firm-level, non-diversifying productivity risk: recalibrate theta_eps/sigma_eps and the project count so idiosyncratic variance stops being 1/size
proposals.one_line: Make the firm-level eps process persistent and volatile enough to dominate Poisson project-count lumpiness, so that d_i is no longer mechanically proportional to 1/n_live ~ 1/size and the true MVE weight stops being a value-weighted market portfolio in disguise.
proposals.economic_story: This is the head-on answer to the size artifact. eps is the FIRM-level productivity shock and u is the PROJECT-level shock. After the Jun-18 10x cut, the CIR shocks contribute only 2.2% of idiosyncratic return variance (was 69.2%) and 97.8% comes from independent Bernoulli project deaths and arrivals. Because death is a Poisson thinning over the firm's live projects, that residual variance scales as 1/n_live, and n_live IS size (I measured corr(log nlive, log mve) = 0.9871). So d_i ~ 1/size mechanically, 1/d_i ~ size, and w* = Sigma^{-1}mu collapses onto a size-weighted portfolio that ANTI-correlates with the empirical size premium — with no sign bug anywhere. Economically the current calibration says firm-level productivity is essentially deterministic and all firm risk is 'did a plant close this month', which is indefensible: measured firm TFP is highly persistent (annual AR(1) of 0.90-0.95, i.e. theta = -log(0.92) = 0.083/yr, not the coded 0.35) and its within-industry cross-sectional dispersion is large (Syverson 2011: 90-10 TFP ratios near 2, sd(log TFP) ~ 0.3-0.6). The current theta_eps = 0.35 and sigma_eps = 0.02 give a stationary sd(eps) of 0.0239 — a firm-level productivity dispersion of 2.4%, which is off by more than an order of magnitude.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: Two channels, and I am honest that the direct one is weak. (i) DIRECT, WEAK: making d_i dispersed and char-linked makes w*_i = numerator_i/d_i a genuine ratio. But under exact K-factor pricing the D^{-1} tilt is worth only 1/(2 sigma_f^2 beta'D^{-1}beta) = O(1/N) of SR* — the diagnosis-phase span experiment measured 0.19% at N=1000 even with d spanning a 20x range. So this buys almost nothing on its own. (ii) INDIRECT, STRONG: heteroskedastic, char-linked D is a MULTIPLIER on any unspanned premium. In the population span experiment, adding d ~ exp(6 x2) raised the RFF-over-linear ceiling from 1.00 to 1.91 in the presence of a LINEAR unspanned alpha and from 2.88 to 6.37 with a nonlinear one, and cut the linear span's share of SR* from 1.00 to 0.31. The reason is that 1/d = exp(-linear-in-chars) is a convex function that FM cannot form even when log d is perfectly linear in chars, and the curvature bites in proportion to sd(log d). So the value of this proposal is entirely conditional on Proposal 2 or 6 being adopted.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: Even in the best case for FM, where log d_i is exactly linear in the characteristics (measured R^2 = 0.880 on the 5 raw chars), the object FM needs is 1/d_i = exp(-b'x_i), and FM's span is {a'x}. The best linear approximation to exp(-b'x) over a distribution with sd(b'x) = s has relative L2 error 1 - (s^2 e^{-s^2}... ) rising steeply in s: at the current sd(log d) = 0.664 the linear approximation loses ~5% of the variance of 1/d; at sd(log d) = 1.0 (the real-data value) it loses ~13%; at 1.3 it loses ~21%. FF is worse still: its weight function is mve_i x (2x3 step function), so it can only produce a step approximation to 1/d and, critically, mve_i multiplies EVERY column — FF's weights are structurally proportional to size, which is the very artifact this proposal is trying to remove. DKKM's RFF spans smooth convex functions of the chars directly.

proposals.name: Heterogeneous operating leverage: a firm-specific fixed operating cost per project
proposals.one_line: Give each project a constant flow cost f_i, so that beta_x — currently EXACTLY 1.0 for every firm — becomes 1 + kappa_i x (sales/price)_i /(r+delta), a product of two observable non-size characteristics that loads on gamma_x, the largest price of risk in the model.
proposals.economic_story: The most embarrassing structural fact about KP14 as implemented is that price = VAP + PVGO is homogeneous of degree one in x (panel_functions_kp14.py:165 and 173), so P_{t+1}/P_t has unit x-elasticity for EVERY firm, and sdf_compute_kp14.py:167 makes this structural by factoring Et_x2[t] out of the whole cross-firm block. I confirmed by inspection that all four erets terms (lines 188-197) are proportional to Et_x. The dominant priced shock therefore generates zero cross-sectional dispersion in exposure; the diagnosis measured the leading systematic loading at 0.03581 with a cross-sectional CV of 3.7%. Operating leverage is the canonical, extensively documented fix: a fixed cost of production makes equity a levered claim on revenue, and the leverage is heterogeneous and observable. This is Carlson-Fisher-Giammarino (2004), Zhang (2005), Novy-Marx (2011) — gross profitability, one of the strongest real anomalies, is literally a fixed-cost-intensity proxy — and Donangelo-Gourio-Kehrig-Palacios on labour as a quasi-fixed cost.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: With a flow cost f_i per live project, VAP_i = x_t sum_j K_j^alpha A(eps,u_j) - n_i f_i/(r+delta) (the cost is deterministic and terminates at the idiosyncratic, hence unpriced, death rate delta, so it is discounted at r+delta with no risk adjustment). The x-elasticity of price is then beta_x,i = [gross x-linear part]/P_i = 1 + f_i n_i /((r+delta) P_i). Writing f_i n_i = kappa_i x Revenue_i, beta_x,i = 1 + kappa_i x (Rev_i/P_i)/(r+delta) — EXACTLY a product of the observable fixed-cost intensity kappa_i (gross-margin char) and the observable sales-to-price ratio. Expected returns become rp_i = gamma_x sigma_x dt x beta_x,i + alph gamma_z sigma_z dt x share_i, so the entire cross-sectional dispersion generated here loads on gamma_x = 0.69, the model's dominant price of risk, rather than on the weak z channel.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: The target is bilinear in two characteristics, NEITHER of which is size. FM's weight function is a fixed linear functional a'x (fama_functions.py:158-160 builds P = X pinvh(X'X) with X = [1, chars]); the product kappa x (Rev/P) is orthogonal to that span. FF has exactly one interaction available — every one of its factors is a value-weighted 2x3 sort of a single characteristic against the SIZE median split (fama_functions.py:70, 82-104) — so it produces size x kappa and size x salesprice, never kappa x salesprice. DKKM's RFF spans the product directly: the diagnosis measured that 86.7% of the coded RFF feature variance lies in the 21-dimensional quadratic span of the characteristics, which contains every pairwise product. This is the second nonlinearity (with Proposal 3's bm x age) that the CURRENT estimator configuration can already reach without touching GAMMA_GRID.

RESULTING BETA_X DISPERSION. beta_x,i = 1 + kappa_i (Rev_i/P_i)/(r+delta). Rev/VAP = 1/A_0 = 0.2297 and VAP/P = 1 - share ~ 0.45 post-Proposal-1, so Rev/P ~ 0.103. With r+delta = 0.15: beta_x = 1 + kappa x 0.689. At the mean kappa = 0.30 that is beta_x = 1.207. The cross-sectional sd has two sources: sd(kappa) x 0.689 = 0.103, plus the dispersion in Rev/P (which spans roughly 0.03 to 0.30 across value and growth firms) contributing kappa_bar x sd(Rev/P)/0.15 = 0.30 x 0.06/0.15 = 0.12. Total sd(beta_x) ~ 0.16, and the two contributions are MULTIPLICATIVE so the joint variation is genuinely bilinear.
RESULTING PREMIUM DISPERSION. gamma_x sigma_x x sd(beta_x) = 0.0897 x 0.16 = 1.44%/yr of cross-sectional expected-return dispersion, entirely from the beta_x channel. For reference the current model has ZERO from this channel and the correctly-repaired z channel gives 0.25%/yr at the current share dispersion or ~1.8%/yr post-Proposal-1. So this roughly doubles the interpretable cross-section, and does so on a bilinear object.
WHY NOT LOWER (r+delta). Halving delta to 0.05 raises the multiplier from 0.689 to 1.03 (a 50% amplification) and is defensible (equipment plus structures depreciate at 6-8%/yr), but it also doubles mean project age and therefore interacts with Proposal 3; treat it as a second-stage knob.
proposals.predicted_effect: DKKM/FM Sharpe ratio 1.15-1.30x standalone AT THE CODED BANDWIDTH — this is the only proposal here that delivers a measurable gap without also rescaling GAMMA_GRID, because the required nonlinearity is exactly quadratic. FF should IMPROVE relative to its current position (a gross-margin sort is a real factor) but stay below FM. max_sr rises by roughly sqrt(1 + (1.44/0.25)^2 x small) — modest, since beta_x dispersion is an aggregate-risk channel and does not scale with N. HJD: modest improvement in separation. Combined with Proposal 2 the two are close to orthogonal (one adds priced dimensions in technology space, the other adds a bilinear loading on the neutral shock), so expect them to compound multiplicatively rather than additively.
risks: This is the one proposal that genuinely breaks the x-homogeneity that sdf_compute_kp14.py:167 exploits. That single line currently carries the entire cross-firm block; splitting P' into an x-proportional and an x-independent piece triples the number of outer products and requires new closed forms for E[n' Q'] and E[n'^2] on the diagonal. Budget a careful re-derivation and re-run the two commented-out single-pair test blocks at sdf_compute_kp14.py:148-159 and 231-254, which are exactly the right regression tests.

With a fixed cost, a newly arriving project can have negative NPV, so the firm should decline it — a free-boundary problem in eps that kp14_fd.py cannot solve as written. Avoid it by capping kappa at 0.60 so that projects are always accepted at every eps in the realized support, and ASSERT this in the simulation.

Equity can go to zero or negative for a high-kappa firm in a bad eps state, producing the same zero/negative-book singularity already documented for KP14. Add the same book>0 style filter on price>0 to the keep mask at sdf_compute_kp14.py:269.

gamma_x sigma_x = 8.97%/yr is a level effect common to all firms; scaling it by beta_x with mean 1.207 raises the average equity premium to 10.8%/yr. Rescale gamma_x to 0.69/1.207 = 0.572 if you want to hold the market premium fixed — but note that gamma_x also enters CONST and hence A_0..A_3 (config.py:264-268) and KP14_RHO, so this triggers a re-solve.
proposals.implementation_cost: sdf_compute stays O(N^2) per month — the added blocks are three more rank-1 outer products (E[Q']E[n'], E[n']E[n'], and their transposes) plus corrected diagonals. The second moment remains exactly analytic: project death is Bernoulli(delta dt) independent across projects and arrivals are Poisson, so E[n'], E[n'^2] and E[n'Q'] all have elementary closed forms. No PDE re-solve is needed — the fixed cost enters G only as an additive analytic constant from the two-state Markov chain, and A_0..A_3 are untouched.

proposals.name: HIGH RISK / HIGH REWARD: a persistent, mean-reverting demand wedge on price whose fundamental anchor is nonlinear in the characteristics
proposals.one_line: Let the observed price be the KP14 fundamental value times exp(w_it) with w an OU noise-trader/demand wedge; the resulting alpha is the price-versus-fundamentals gap, which is only recoverable by inverting a nonlinear map from many characteristics to fundamental value — the AIPT near-arbitrage that DKKM's theory says is the ONLY thing that makes complexity pay.
proposals.economic_story: Every diagnosis agent reached the same conclusion from a different direction: KP14 is a frictionless rational-expectations economy in which mu is BY CONSTRUCTION minus the covariance with the model's own SDF, and under exact K-factor pricing with N=1000 the maximum Sharpe is attained to within 0.2% by any well-diversified portfolio with the right factor exposure. The population span experiment measured RFF-over-linear ceiling ratios of 0.994 under exact factor pricing versus 8.6 with a nonlinear non-risk premium and 21 with a nonlinear premium plus heteroskedastic D. DKKM's own Theorem 3 says the same thing: complexity pays iff the eigenvalue distribution of E[FF'] is flat, which requires many quasi-orthogonal priced directions, and their 'APT calibration' (concentrated eigenvalues) reproduces the BOP null result exactly, including the harm at light shrinkage. The economically standard way to get a component of expected returns that is not a covariance is a demand or belief wedge: noise-trader demand (De Long-Shleifer-Summers-Waldmann), inelastic markets and slow-moving capital (Gabaix-Koijen, Duffie), or segmented clienteles with a different marginal investor. Applied to KP14, the natural story is a growth-option clientele: retail and momentum flows chase high-PVGO-share, high-idiosyncratic-volatility names, pushing their prices away from fundamentals by an amount that decays over several years (McLean-Pontiff, Chordia-Subrahmanyam-Tong on anomaly decay).
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: Set P_it^obs = P_it^fund exp(w_it - 0.5 Var_inf(w)) with dw_i = -kappa_w w_i dt + sigma_w dB_i^w, B^w independent across firms and of all fundamentals. The conditional expected gross return acquires the factor a_i = E_t[e^{w'}]/e^{w} = exp(-(1-e^{-kappa_w dt}) w_i + 0.5 s^2), so alpha_i = -(1 - e^{-kappa_w dt}) w_i ~ -kappa_w dt w_i. Because the wedge is idiosyncratic, its contribution to the squared maximum Sharpe is alpha' D^{-1} alpha ~ N x E[alpha^2/d], which GROWS WITH N — this is the near-arbitrage that no finite number of factor-mimicking portfolios can span. Now, w_i is not directly observed, but log P^obs = log book - log bm and log P^fund = log book + h(chars), so w_i = -log bm_i - h(chars_i) where h is the model's own map from fundamentals to the value-to-book multiple. Under Proposals 3 and 5 that map is genuinely nonlinear: h depends on the vintage composition (age), the arrival regime and lambda_f (invint), the project count, the fixed-cost intensity, and the PVGO share. Recovering alpha therefore requires inverting a nonlinear multi-characteristic map — the precise object DKKM's random-feature ridge is designed for, and the precise object FM's single linear functional is not.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: FM's stock-weight function is a'x, a FIXED linear functional. It can only produce the linear projection of -log bm - h(x) onto the characteristics, i.e. it captures alpha only to the extent that h is linear. The residual, 1 - R^2 of h on the linear span, is pure lost Sharpe for FM, and because the alpha channel is a near-arbitrage that scales as sqrt(N) rather than being bounded by the factor Sharpe, that loss is very large in squared-Sharpe terms. FF is strictly worse: alpha_i has no reason to be monotone in any single characteristic, its 2x3 tercile sorts throw away within-tercile variation (which is where most of the alpha dispersion lives, since w is continuous), and its weights are all proportional to mve so it cannot even hold an equal-weighted position in the mispriced names. Note this is also the ONE proposal for which the '25 size/BM portfolios' pricing test would gain real power, because alpha would be a genuinely non-monotone, interactive function rather than a repackaging of size and value.

proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation:
TARGET THE NEAR-ARBITRAGE SHARPE FIRST, THEN BACK OUT THE PARAMETERS. DKKM's real-data complex model attains an annualized tangency Sharpe of 3.7, i.e. 3.7/sqrt(12) = 1.068/month. If that comes from N=1000 quasi-independent alphas, the per-stock monthly information ratio is 1.068/sqrt(1000) = 0.0338. With idiosyncratic monthly vol of 5% that implies sd(alpha) = 0.0338 x 0.05 = 0.00169/month = 2.03%/yr. Now alpha_i = (1 - e^{-kappa_w dt}) w_i, so sd(alpha) = (1 - e^{-kappa_w/12}) x SD_W. Setting kappa_w x SD_W = 12 x 0.00169 = 0.0203/yr and choosing SD_W = 0.15 (a 15% log cross-sectional valuation error, at the conservative end of the Rhodes-Kropf-Robinson-Viswanathan misvaluation decomposition, which puts firm-specific error at 0.3-0.4) gives kappa_w = 0.0203/0.15 = 0.135/yr, a half-life of log 2 / 0.135 = 5.1 years. That is right in the range of measured anomaly decay for slow-moving, value-like mispricing. Then SIGMA_W = SD_W sqrt(2 kappa_w) = 0.15 x sqrt(0.27) = 0.0779.
SANITY CHECK ON THE INDUCED VOLATILITY. The wedge adds sigma_w x sqrt(dt) = 0.0779 x 0.2887 = 2.25%/month of extra idiosyncratic return volatility, i.e. it raises idio vol from 3.3% to 4.0%/month (with Proposal 4) — a 21% increase, which is if anything a move TOWARD real-data levels (~10%/month), not away.
HOW MUCH OF THE ALPHA IS LEARNABLE. alpha_i = kappa_w dt (log bm_i + h(chars_i)). The learnable fraction equals the R^2 of h on whatever function class the estimator can express. With Proposals 3 and 5 in place, log(P^fund/book) is a smooth function of (age, nproj, invint, roe, grossmargin, salesprice, share) — I would expect R^2 near 0.9 for a rich nonlinear basis and perhaps 0.5-0.6 for a linear one, which is precisely the wedge that produces the DKKM advantage. Diagnose this BEFORE running the estimator: regress the true w_i on [1, chars] and on a degree-3 polynomial in the chars and compare R^2. If the linear R^2 is above 0.85, this proposal will not deliver and you should enrich h first.
proposals.predicted_effect: This is the only proposal that can plausibly reach the real-data 3-5x target on its own. Rough accounting with SD_W = 0.15, kappa_w = 0.135: the wedge contributes alpha'D^{-1}alpha = N x (sd(alpha)/sd_idio)^2 = 1000 x (0.00169/0.040)^2 = 1.79 to the monthly squared Sharpe, versus the factor contribution of about 0.05 (0.223/month squared) post-Proposal-1. So SR* goes to sqrt(1.84) = 1.36/month = 4.7/yr. If DKKM recovers 70% of the alpha's variance and FM 40%, SR_DKKM = sqrt(0.70 x 1.79 + 0.05) = 1.14/month and SR_FM = sqrt(0.40 x 1.79 + 0.05) = 0.86/month, a 1.33x gap; if the split is 85%/30% it is sqrt(1.57)/sqrt(0.59) = 1.63x; if h is strongly nonlinear so the split is 90%/15% it is 2.4x. HJD: with SR* = 1.36/month, sd(sdf_ret) = 1.006 x 1.36/2.85 = 0.480 and the zero-portfolio HJD is 0.802; the FM-to-DKKM range is roughly 0.55 to 0.36, comfortably separable. Pricing errors on the 25 size/BM portfolios finally acquire power because alpha is genuinely non-monotone.
risks: IT CHANGES WHAT 'TRUE' MEANS. The paper's whole framing is that these are structural, frictionless models and 'the truth' is the model's own SDF. Introducing a wedge means the true MVE portfolio is partly harvesting mispricing, and a referee will ask whether the exercise has become circular — 'complexity pays because we assumed a nonlinear alpha'. The strongest defence is to frame it as SEGMENTED MARKETS / heterogeneous marginal investors rather than irrationality, and to note that DKKM's AIPT is explicitly an approximate-arbitrage theory in which alpha is not a covariance. Be prepared for this to be the single most contested modelling choice in the paper.

The near-arbitrage Sharpe scales as sqrt(N), so the result becomes an artifact of N=1000. Report the same table at N=250, 500, 1000 and show the DKKM/FM RATIO is stable even though the levels are not. If the ratio moves with N you have measured diversification, not complexity.

Unbundling term4 at sdf_compute_kp14.py:162-165 is the riskiest code surgery in this whole set, because the existing expression -outer(cf/P, cf/P) is a double-counting correction that only works when the two legs share the same normalization. Rederive the four-way expansion from scratch and validate against the commented-out single-pair test blocks at lines 148-159 and 231-254 before trusting a single number.

w must be independent of the characteristics ex ante or the model is circular (chars depend on price which depends on w). The OU-with-zero-mean specification is safe; a specification where the wedge's long-run level depends on chars is NOT, and should be avoided.

If SD_W is set too high the wedge dominates the fundamentals and bm ceases to carry any information about share, which would destroy the Proposal 3 channel. Keep SD_W below about 0.25 and check that corr(bm, true PVGO share) stays above 0.5.
proposals.implementation_cost: sdf_compute stays O(N^2): every wedge adjustment is a rank-1 rescaling by outer(a, a) plus a diagonal replacement, and both a_i and b_i are elementary lognormal OU moments. The second moment remains exactly analytic — no quadrature, no re-solve of kp14_fd.py or integ_kp14.py, because the wedge is orthogonal to eps, u, x, z and the arrival process. The cost is entirely in the algebra of unbundling the cash-flow terms and in re-validating against the existing single-pair tests.
